newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the the U.S. weekly jobless claims and third-quarter productivity data, dealers said on Thursday.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended November 30 is forecast to be around 337,000 compared with 342,000 reported in the previous week.
Productivity for the third-quarter is expected to be revised downwards to a 0.1 percent decline against a 0.2 percent increase in the previous quarter.

"The market was quietly steady in the morning on some position adjustments. The market is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims and third-quarter productivity figures," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are off market expectations, there won't be much impact. Some people are also waiting for this Friday's issue of the monthly employment report," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday, weekend and week-fixed were unchanged from Wednesday's common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, six-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
